claim: AlphaZero mastered chess in 4 hours
verdict: It did pass Stockfish, but Stockfish ran with weakened settings.
detail: AlphaZero beat Stockfish 8 with 28 wins and no losses. Chess experts noted Stockfish had a small hash table and no opening book.

claim: GPT-4 scored in the 90th percentile on the bar exam
verdict: Closer to the 48th–69th percentile against typical test-takers.
detail: A peer-reviewed re-analysis found OpenAI compared against a February pool skewed to repeat takers. Against first-time takers it was about the 62nd percentile.

claim: GNoME discovered 2.2 million new materials
verdict: Chemists found little evidence the compounds are novel and useful.
detail: A UC Santa Barbara review found scant evidence of compounds that are new, credible and useful. DeepMind stands by the paper.

claim: A robot lab made 41 new compounds in 17 days
verdict: Corrected: the compounds were new to the lab, not to science.
detail: Outside chemists found most products were misidentified. The paper's correction now reports 36 of 57 targets and drops the novelty claim.

claim: Gemini responds to live video and voice in real time
verdict: Google admitted the demo used still frames and text prompts.
detail: The hands-on video was edited. Google confirmed it was not real time and that the voice prompts were dubbed in afterwards.

claim: Klarna's AI assistant does the work of 700 agents
verdict: Klarna later said quality suffered and hired humans back.
detail: The CEO said cost had been too big a factor and service quality dropped. Klarna began hiring human agents again in 2025.

claim: Devin, the first AI software engineer, completes real Upwork jobs
verdict: Critics showed the demo task wasn't what the client asked for.
detail: A developer's breakdown found Devin did different work than requested and took hours on a 30-minute task. Cognition said Devin often makes mistakes.

claim: Just Walk Out stores run on computer vision
verdict: Reports say 1,000 workers in India reviewed most sales. Amazon denies it.
detail: The Information reported 700 of every 1,000 sales needed human review in 2022. Amazon says the team mainly labels data for training.

claim: AI upgrades saved Amazon 4,500 developer-years
verdict: Amazon's own estimate; no independent audit.
detail: Amazon says Java upgrades went from 50 days to hours per app. The figures come from internal estimates.

claim: AI CUDA Engineer makes code 10–100x faster
verdict: The system cheated its own tests. Sakana apologized.
detail: Users found a 3x slowdown. Sakana admitted the model exploited the evaluation code and revised its paper.

claim: AI co-scientist matched 10 years of lab work in 2 days
verdict: Its top hypothesis matched the lab's finding, later published in Cell.
detail: The Imperial College team had unpublished data; Google confirmed no leak. Other models failed the same test.

claim: Builder.ai's AI, Natasha, builds apps for you
verdict: Reporting found about 700 engineers did the work. The company collapsed.
detail: Builder.ai entered insolvency in May 2025. Reports say engineers coded projects presented as AI-made.

claim: AI diagnoses complex cases 4x better than doctors
verdict: The peer-reviewed gap is about 2.3x, against restricted doctors.
detail: Doctors worked without references, colleagues or specialists. The Science version reports 83% vs 36%.

claim: AI tools made experienced developers 19% slower
verdict: A randomized trial with 246 real tasks found it.
detail: Developers believed AI sped them up by 20%. The authors warn it covers early-2025 tools and expert devs on familiar code.

claim: An AI won gold at the Math Olympiad
verdict: DeepMind's proofs were graded by official IMO coordinators.
detail: Gemini Deep Think scored 35 of 42 in contest time. OpenAI's same score was graded by former medalists, not the IMO.

claim: 95% of generative AI pilots fail
verdict: Critics say the number isn't explained and measures something narrower.
detail: The figure comes from a funnel of task-specific tools reaching production. The report calls itself preliminary.

claim: GPT-5 solved 10 open Erdős problems
verdict: It found existing solutions. The post was deleted.
detail: The site's maintainer said 'open' only meant he didn't know of a solution. GPT-5 had located papers that already solved them.

claim: Agents built a web browser from scratch in a week
verdict: It renders pages, but builds failed and code reuse was questioned.
detail: Over 1M lines were written. Reviewers found failing builds; critics said it leaned on Servo, which Cursor denies.

claim: An amateur solved Erdős #1196 with one prompt
verdict: Mathematicians checked it and it was verified in Lean.
detail: The 60-year-old problem is marked solved. Experts said the approach surprised them.

claim: AI cut a 231-day migration to 13 days
verdict: Self-reported; 231 days is an estimate, not a measurement.
detail: 33 API endpoints were moved using Claude Code. No independent check of the numbers.

claim: Bun was rewritten from Zig to Rust in 11 days
verdict: It shipped as Bun 1.4 and passed the full test suite.
detail: 64 Claude agents ported ~535,000 lines. Zig's creator called it unreviewed.

claim: Claude agents discovered a new enzyme system
verdict: The system is real, but its function is unknown.
detail: Found in 21 hours by ~950 agents. A similar system was found earlier at Stanford, and 10 reruns missed it.
